newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil market focused on French diesel buying.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil market focused on French diesel buying.

text.p: Discussion in the NWE gas oil market was centred on diesel on Monday, with active buying interest seen into France.
Offers were heard at May IPE +13/+14 a tonne cif Le Havre, with best bids at $11.50 for delivery by end-April. A UK refiner sold a cargo on a confidential basis but no other deals were reported.
"It's a pretty keen market, that's where all the attention is today," said one trader.
The German market was less active, with diesel cargoes were talked around May IPE +$9.50/$10.50 cif Hamburg.
On the barge market, two 0.05 percent sulphur parcels were traded at May IPE $9.50, one fob Flushing and the other fob Rotterdam-Amsterdam.
Heating oil barges changed hands at May IPE +50 cents and +25 cents, with offers at +50 cents and bids at screen flat towards the end of the day.
Traders said that offers of IPE delivery material from Antwerp at $1 under the May IPE contract were dragging the market lower.
"Even with the freight that's cheaper than Rotterdam material," said one trader.

Heating oil cargoes were thinly talked on Monday. Some discussion on DIN was heard with prompt premiums at May IPE +$2/$3.50 cif Hamburg, while Russian cargoes were bid at May +$1 with supplies scarce.
May IPE futures closed $1.50 a tonne higher at $165, off the session high of $165.75.
